While we stood around him, and certain sisters were speaking with me about it, behold, my heart suddenly melted and I was almost caught up into ecstasy. And behold, a great brightness shone in the pyx; and I looked within, [Col. 0140D] although it was still closed, and the appearance of true flesh was visible in it. I tremble in relating these things, as I trembled when I saw them then. God is my witness that in all these things I have spoken nothing through invention or in pursuit of my own glory.

39. You asked me by letter, brother, concerning your patrons, namely the martyrs of the Church of Bonn, Cassius and Florentius, that on the day of their feast [Note: [Col. 0139D] Saints Cassius, Florentius, and Mallusius, of the company of St Gereon—whose passion is celebrated at Cologne on 10 October—are said to have escaped by flight to Bonn, where they were discovered and slain, on an uncertain day. The elevation of these same saints, performed about the year 1076 under Archbishop Reinold, is celebrated on 2 May. This feast is called the common feast-day of all of them, 10 October.] I should render them some [Col. 0141A] service, if perhaps they too might deign to show themselves to me. And I did what I could: in their honor I read fifty psalms that day after Matins. There also my tempter extinguished the candle which I held in my hand.

After this, about the third hour, I entered ecstasy without pain and saw three men in the realm of light, adorned with palms and with crowns marked red upon their foreheads. Two of them stood joined together, while the third stood a little apart [Note: [Col. 0141] Namely because the body of Mallusius, who is not named here, had perhaps been taken to some other church.].

On the following day, at Vespers, while I was in ecstasy in the usual manner—for it was Saturday—I asked the Lord to show me again those patrons of yours. I was troubled because I had not distinctly recognized who the two were about whom you had asked, since I had seen three. [Col. 0141B] The Lord delayed hearing me for a time, so that I feared I had asked this contrary to the Lord’s will. Trembling, I said: “Lord, if it is your will that what I asked should happen, let it happen; but if not, let it not happen.”

Immediately I saw two most lovable men coming forth from the company of martyrs, with the signs mentioned above; and they came to stand in the middle before the presence of the throne. Awakening joyfully, I immediately took up these words:

> “These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands, shining before the Lord, ruler of the whole earth.”

After this, on the feast of the Eleven Thousand Holy Virgins, I saw a great multitude of virgins, all distinguished by palms of victory, crowns marked upon their foreheads, and beautiful, splendid hair.

[Col. 0141C] 40. On the vigil of All Saints, at Vespers, I came into the stillness of ecstasy. Then, as usual, it seemed to me that my spirit was found aloft; and I saw a door opened in heaven, and such a multitude of saints as I had never before seen. What I remember telling you concerning the holy Trinity was then made known to me for the second time.

But on the day of the solemnity itself, at Vespers, again caught up into ecstasy, I saw standing before me what seemed to be a most lovable boy, clothed in a white garment and girded. I said: “Who are you, my Lord?” He nodded for me to be silent; and I said: “May the good angel of the Lord, who was with Jacob, be with me in the land of my pilgrimage, and may God bless my ways.” Immediately [Col. 0141D] I seemed to be lifted aloft, and I heard voices singing a most delightful song.

41. After this, on the day when, according to the Church’s custom, the common commemoration of the faithful departed was observed, during the time of the divine sacrifice, I saw, as though toward the south, a very high mountain, and beside it a deep valley, exceedingly dreadful. It was full of black fires, as though covered over and unable to send flame high upward. There I saw innumerable tormenting spirits and souls delivered into their power, horribly and lamentably shaken, dragged about, and afflicted beyond measure in countless ways. I discerned no forms either [Col. 0142A] in these or in those; I understood only that the former were tormenting and the latter being tormented.

Far from there, toward the east, I saw a most glorious building, as though surrounded by three walls. Within it were variously distinguished dwellings, and the splendor of immeasurable light illuminated everything. Around it there appeared a most delightful beauty of trees, grass, and flowers. The place which seemed to lie between this building and the aforesaid valley was entirely occupied by very harsh, as though scorched, thorns.

As I watched, behold, a great multitude of white-robed people rose from the valley and seemed to make their way through the midst of that impassable thicket, with great haste and much effort, toward the building mentioned above; and at last, [Col. 0142B] having arrived, they entered it. But some of them chose a path outside the briars and arrived without labor. This passage took place many times and at intervals.

42. Nor do I wish you to be ignorant, brother, concerning one of our friends, whom we loved as a father. On the anniversary of his death, after I had done certain things for his deliverance which had been shown to me in a vision, I saw him during the sacrifice standing before me in a white garment, with a handsome young man beside him, clothed in white and girded. After he had devoutly lifted hands and eyes toward heaven before me, as though giving thanks, he turned from me and went with his companion on the journey as far as that building which I described above. Watching their paths, [Col. 0142C] I did not cease seeing them until they entered there.

What more shall I tell you about visions of the saints, except that each of them, on his or her feast-day—as has been said—deigned to console my soul?

43. During Advent I saw a certain splendid building, surrounded by one wall; and in its midst a tower of such height that its summit seemed to pierce heaven. Since this frequently appeared to me in this way, it happened on one Sunday, as I returned from ecstasy, that I suddenly took up a prayer of this kind:

> “Lord Jesus Christ, merciful and ready to hear, show me, your unworthy servant, what this city is which you have shown me.”

Immediately these words of answer were placed upon my lips:

> “This is the heavenly Jerusalem, which is being built [Col. 0142D] as a city whose summit reaches to the heavens.”

After this, with the feast of the Nativity of the Lord approaching, I prepared myself for my customary transports of mind two days before the feast-day. When the evening of the solemnity of the Nativity came, I at last entered the stillness of ecstasy. I felt myself as though lifted aloft and saw a door opened in heaven. That venerable mystery which I had seen on the feast of All Saints was now shown to me for the third time.

Delighting in the abundance of the sweetness of my God, I at last returned to myself and immediately burst forth in these words:

> “With desire I have desired to see [Col. 0143A] the Lord God my Savior, and I have seen him, and behold, my soul has been saved.”

I remained in prayer throughout the night and could not give my body to sleep because of the excessive brightness of the light which I beheld the whole night. For I continually saw opened in great joy that door which I had previously been unable to behold except in mental transport; and its light appeared tenfold brighter than in the previous visions.

44. When preparations were being made for the celebration of the first Mass, which was to be sung amid the Matins office, I saw a ray of great brightness stretching down from that same door to the altar of the oratory. When “The book of the generation” was begun [Note: [Col. 0143D] According to the monastic-Benedictine use, feasts have twelve lessons; but on the feast of the Nativity, four Gospels are read at the third Nocturn, the first being “The beginning of the Holy Gospel according to Matthew,” and the other three being those prescribed by the Roman use.], behold, the most glorious Queen of Heaven, accompanied by a great host of angels, descended by the same ray [Col. 0143B] and stood at the priest’s right hand, wearing upon her head a crown of the greatest and most delightful splendor.

When the Gospel had ended and, according to custom, the antiphon “O Lady of the world” was sung, she rose with her company and returned through the aforesaid ray of light to her seat. Though I remained in ecstasy throughout that entire time, I nevertheless did not cease most devoutly to invoke her.

Two splendid youths had descended by the aforesaid ray and remained near the altar ministers from the beginning of the Mass until its end; and at the second Mass there were another two. One stood at the priest’s side, and the other beside the deacon when he announced the Gospel. Regarding [Col. 0143C] the one beside the deacon, I thought inwardly that he was one of our deacons who was attending Mass, and that he was wearing an alb—which indeed was not the case—and standing to minister. Yet I was doubtful because this one appeared white and curly-haired, whereas the other was black. Then he turned his face toward me as though offended, and immediately these words were impressed upon my heart: “I am the Angel of the Covenant.”

Amid all this, I also saw the dove sitting upon the Lord’s sacrifice on the altar.

45. On the following day, during the divine office, I saw Blessed Stephen the protomartyr in heavenly brightness, exceedingly splendid and distinguished by the marks of martyrdom and the diaconate. That same day at Vespers I saw Blessed John the Evangelist standing before the throne, [Col. 0143D] adorned in a most white garment and a golden stole in priestly fashion. I looked toward the place where I was accustomed to see the four Evangelists, and I saw three animals; but the place of the Eagle appeared empty.

On the day of the Innocents, during the divine office, I saw a high and splendid mountain, and upon its summit a white Lamb, most lovable, bearing on its back the sign of the Lord’s cross. A great multitude of martyrs followed him, with [Col. 0144A] palms and crowns marked red. I thought to myself that these were those blessed children killed for the Lord Jesus. Yet I wondered at this: no sign of childhood appeared in them, for all seemed to possess the fullness of youthful age.

On the Circumcision of the Lord and the Epiphany [Note: [Col. 0143D] The year 1154 had Sunday letter C; [Col. 0144D] accordingly the beginning of the year fell on Friday and Epiphany on Tuesday.], I saw the Sunday vision, but more clearly on the Epiphany. Then, too, at First Vespers, I saw three crowned kings standing before the throne. Coming forward, they worshipped on bended knees before the Son of Man; removing their crowns from their heads, they offered them into his hands, and received them again from him. During the day at Mass I saw the same three again, worshipping before the Lord Jesus; and they seemed to place in his hands certain small bright gifts, I know not what.

[Col. 0144B] 46. On the Purification of the most glorious Mother Mary, at Mass, after the Gospel had been read, I entered ecstasy and saw: behold, my lady descended by a ray of light and stood at the priest’s right hand, and beside her was an aged and venerable man, with a long gray beard. When the sisters had offered candles into the priest’s hands, she returned to the heights. And behold, a great host of distinguished maidens, with splendid candles, came out to meet her. After they had remained a little while in this outer light, they returned with her to the higher regions, following her joyfully.

That same day at Vespers, while I was in ecstasy and saw her again in heavenly glory, I most devoutly invoked her aid and with all [Col. 0144C] diligence entrusted myself and my loved ones to her. At the end of my prayer I added: “My lady, what may I hope from you?” She seemed to answer: “You, and all who place their trust in me, may hope for good favor from me.”

God has also made his mercies wonderful toward me, my brother, since you recently departed from me, and has done these things for me.

47. It happened on the first Sunday of the solemn Fast [Note: [Col. 0144D] The same year Easter was celebrated on 4 April; accordingly the first Sunday of Lent fell on 21 February.], at First Vespers, that I entered a transport of mind. I saw a white wheel revolving in the air with marvelous speed, and on its summit a little white bird holding itself with great difficulty lest it be whirled around by the wheel’s force. Several times it slipped a little from the summit toward the lower parts, then rose to the top; and thus it struggled for a long time, [Col. 0144D] slipping and rising again by turns.

After this I saw a high mountain, very bitter, and the wheel was carried over it and revolved there again as before, while the little bird clinging to it persevered in its struggle. I was greatly wondering what these things might signify, and with great desire sought from the Lord an understanding of the vision. Having received some little understanding, I returned from ecstasy and immediately took up these words:

> “Narrow and strait is the way [Col. 0145A] that leads to life, Lord; who will walk through it?”

I added:

> “The one who guards his life from carnal desires and has no deceit in his tongue.”

And I added: “Lord, what shall I do?” Again these words of response came upon my lips:

> “If you wish to walk as I walked, consider my footsteps; do not turn aside to the right or to the left, but follow me, and thus you will arrive. For I said: ‘I am the way, the truth, and the life; if anyone enters through me, he shall be saved and shall find pasture’” (John 10).

48. After this, on Monday, I again entered ecstasy and saw the aforesaid vision as before, but more fully, because I also saw a ladder standing above the wheel, of such height that its summit [Col. 0145B] seemed to pierce heaven. Its side-posts appeared to be stone and triangular; its rungs differed from one another by most diverse and beautiful intervals. I retained this in memory: the first was white as snow, but the second red as glowing iron.

On the following day I again saw all the things just described, and beside the wheel a figure of a man standing. His head seemed golden, his hair like clean white wool; his eyes most bright and very beautiful; his breast and arms, which he held outstretched in the form of a cross, had a most pure brilliance, like the brightest silver. In his right hand he held a green branch of a tree, pleasant to look upon, and in his left a shining wheel [Col. 0145C] marked by the variegation of a rainbow. His belly appeared bronze, his thighs steel, his legs iron, and his feet earthen. All these things appeared to me frequently during Lent.

49. It happened on the Sunday immediately after the feast of Blessed Gregory [Note: [Col. 0145D] This was the fourth Sunday of Lent, occurring on the second day after the feast, 14 March.], while I was in ecstasy and saw the visions I am accustomed to see on Sundays, that I saw that eminent teacher in the heavenly places, full of glory and lovely brightness, resembling the glory of the most holy bishops Martin and Nicholas. On his head, as I had seen them also wear, he had a certain venerable diadem such as bishops are said to wear.

At the same hour I saw the aforesaid vision, [Col. 0145D] and burned with great desire to understand what I saw, especially what the figure of the man signified; for I understood something concerning the rest. Therefore I most devoutly asked that blessed man of God to obtain for me from the Lord the understanding of the vision which I desired. Turning to me, he answered with these words:

> “You cannot understand what these things signify; but tell the teachers who read the Scriptures: they know.”

Now therefore, most beloved brother, I beg you to undertake this labor: search the divine Scriptures and try to discover from them a fitting interpretation [Col. 0146A] of this vision, for perhaps it has been reserved for you by the Lord.

50. Seven days before the Annunciation of the Lord [Note: [Col. 0145D] Therefore, from 18 March.], I fell ill and took to bed, weak in my whole body, so that I could scarcely take any nourishment for my body. I remained in this condition until the [Note: [Col. 0146D] That is, until the feast of St Benedict, or the following day, the twenty-second.] third day before the feast.

That day, about None, I began to have in my mouth a liquid like a honeycomb; its sweetness refreshed me as though I had received sufficient food. I was strengthened throughout my body and poured forth abundant sweat, in which I remained until the following day. About the time of Mass I entered a transport of mind, and it seemed to me as though my spirit were drawn out from my body and lifted on high.

[Col. 0146B] In that transport I saw heaven opened, and the Lord Jesus coming with countless thousands into this region of the air. He had neither form nor beauty; rather, he appeared so pitiable, as though he had been freshly crucified. After he had shown the whole world the cross upon which he had hung and the wounds of his Passion, as though wet with fresh blood, he cried in a loud and most terrible voice:

> “Such things I endured for you; but what have you endured for me?”

51. Two distinct hosts of innumerable people stood beside him, one on the right and the other on the left. Those on the right seemed surrounded by immeasurable light; among them the Virgin of virgins, the most glorious Mother of God, Mary, appeared preeminent. There [Col. 0146C] I clearly perceived the several ranks of all ecclesiastics; among them I delighted to recognize our venerable father, Blessed Benedict, with his monastic company.

But those on the left were surrounded by dense and dreadful darkness, so that I could scarcely distinguish their different kinds. The ruler of this most wretched people was that great and terrible king of pride; nearest him stood Judas, Pilate, and the crucifiers of the Lord. Alas, how many clergy, how many men and women of our own order, full of shame, I recognized there!

When I had seen everything, the Judge of all said to those on the right: “Come, blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world” (Matt. 25); but to those on the left: “Go, cursed ones, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels” (ibid.). Immediately the former followed the Lord with most joyful eagerness to the shining dwellings; but the latter, full of sorrow and confusion, were plunged with their father, the prince of demons, into the deepest darkness.

52. Immediately after this I was restored to myself, and with abundant weeping I first burst forth in these words:

> “Deliver me, Lord, from eternal death on that dreadful day [Col. 0147A] when the heavens and the earth shall be moved.”

And I added:

> “I believe that my Redeemer lives, and on the last day I shall rise from the earth, and in my flesh I shall see God my Savior.”

On the feast-day itself, while I was again in my transport during the divine sacrifice, the Passion of our Savior was presented to my eyes: how he was stripped of his garment by wicked people, scourged, and finally fastened to the cross. Yet I did not then see separately all that was done to him in the Passion, as I did afterward on Good Friday. When I ceased to see these things, I saw my lady standing in heavenly brightness and received from her the revelation of a certain matter which I do not yet wish to make known.

## CHAPTER IV. The Saint Sees the Mysteries of the Passion, Resurrection, Ascension, Pentecost, and Certain Other Things in This Year

[Col. 0147B]

53. After this, on Palm Sunday [Note: [Col. 0147D] Palm Sunday in the year 1154 fell on 28 March.], at First Vespers, while the sisters were saying the responsory, “Pilate entered,” and had proceeded as far as the words, “Let him be crucified,” I stood among them and entered ecstasy. I saw the Savior as though hanging upon the cross. The same happened to me again at Matins.

During the day at Mass, when the Passion of the Lord was begun, I again entered ecstasy. Then I saw at a distance a pleasant mountain; the Savior descended from it seated on an ass and came toward a great city. At the mountain’s very foot a crowd of people, small and great, met him with green branches of trees. Stripping off their garments, [Col. 0147C] very many of them spread them upon the road along which he was proceeding. Rejoicing, they went with him as far as the gate of the city.

There was a great crowd there and it made room for him. He came through their midst as far as the temple; dismounting, he entered it, and I saw him no further, but returned to myself.

I had earnestly asked my brethren to celebrate the Palm office that day in the meadow before our view, but they could not do so because of flooding streams. Instead, they performed it behind the church, where we were unable to see them. But the Lord regarded the desire of his handmaid, and I saw with the eyes of my mind everything that they did there.

54. After this, at the Mass of the Lord’s Supper, I saw, as I am accustomed to do, everything that was being done about the altar; and [Col. 0147D] while the priest was reciting the canon and elevating the chalice before God, I saw the Lord Jesus above the chalice, as though hanging upon the cross, and blood seemed to flow from his side and feet into the chalice. When evening drew near, I was in the chapel where the rite of the washing of feet was to be celebrated. And when the antiphon *Before the feast day* was begun, I immediately burst into most abundant tears and was carried away in ecstasy.

Then I saw the Lord in the same city into which he had entered on Palm Sunday [Col. 0148A], sitting with his disciples in a house, as though about to dine. As I looked, he rose from the meal; and, laying aside his garments, girded himself with a linen cloth. Taking a basin, he bent his knees before Peter; and immediately Peter sprang up and stood as though terrified. The Lord, while still bowed down, seemed to speak to him; and shortly afterward Peter sat down again. And the Lord washed the feet of each one; then, having resumed his garment, he reclined again and sat as though speaking with them.

After this he rose and went out of the city with them, proceeding toward that mountain from which I had seen him descend. Afterward I saw how the Lord, leaving the disciples, withdrew from them; and, kneeling upon the ground, fell forward in prayer, as though placed in great anguish. I also saw those precious [Col. 0148B] drops of blood running from his most holy flesh to the earth. After praying, he returned to the disciples, whom I saw sleeping. Having addressed them, he returned again to prayer; and this happened three times.

Then, returning to myself, I immediately had these words in my mouth: “Jesus, being in agony, prayed more earnestly, and his sweat became like drops of blood running down to the earth.” And I added: “On the Mount of Olives I prayed to my Father: Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me.”

55. And shortly afterward I again entered into ecstasy. And I saw: behold, the Lord, returning from prayer, took the disciples and came into the garden. Soon afterward Judas came with an armed cohort and, approaching, kissed [Col. 0148C] him; but those who were with him drew back and fell to the ground. Rising, they seized him and dragged him wretchedly, bound, all the way to the city; and I saw the disciples scatter to their hiding places.

Then I returned from ecstasy with words of this kind: “My friend betrayed me with the sign of a kiss, saying: ‘He whom I shall kiss is the one; seize him.’” Thereafter, throughout that entire night, whether I slept or kept watch, I saw how those impious men blasphemed the Lord—beating him, spitting upon him, striking him with blows of the fist and slaps. I did not indeed enter ecstasy, but my whole consciousness was there, and I could attend to nothing else.

In the morning, at the third hour, I entered into ecstasy, in which I remained until about the sixth hour. Then I saw how they clothed [Col. 0148D] him in a purple tunic and wrapped him in a scarlet cloak; and, placing a crown of thorns upon his head, mocked him. After this, stripping him of those garments, they dressed him in his own clothes; placed the cross upon him; and led him outside the city to a certain place, as though ploughed, with no greenery at all. There, stripping him naked, they raised him upon the cross and fastened him to it; they did the same to two others.

[Note: [Col. 0147D] This agrees with the vision of St Bridget, which I discussed in the *Parergon* between the two Lives of St Mary Magdalene de’ Pazzi. It teaches that the Lord was brought upward onto the [Col. 0148D] cross and thus, standing, fastened to it; contrary to the way he is now commonly conceived, including in the visions of more recent female saints, as stretched out upon a cross laid on the ground.]

Then I awoke, and with most abundant tears burst into these words: “Christ [Col. 0149A] the Lord became obedient unto death.” And I added: “Life dies upon the wood. Hell and death are stripped of their spoils.”

[Note: [Col. 0149D] Thus I correct the printed reading, which had *ex morsu* (“from a bite”).]

56. Then, after a short time, the brethren began to celebrate the divine office; and when they had reached the reading of the Passion, I entered ecstasy and again saw the Lord on the cross. At that hour he gave up his spirit, and his neck bent down; his beloved head fell; his knees [Note: [Col. 0149D] This bending of the knees suits a body not stretched most tightly and standing upon some support; it does not suit the manner conceived by St Osanna below, *Life* II, no. 244, who greatly exaggerated, almost above his other pains, the pain felt in the chest from that violent [Col. 0150D] stretching of the arms. This confirms the teaching set out by me in the aforesaid *Parergon*: the words and actions of ecstatics are not to be drawn into historical controversies.] folded; and all his limbs sank downward. Thus the lifeless body hung, more worthy of pity than anything pitiable ever seen by human eyes.

And what, brother, do you think was meanwhile the grief of my soul, when I saw such sufferings and such unworthy contempt inflicted upon the best of men and the one innocent man, who [Col. 0149B] endured everything freely, not for himself but for us? Yet I saw the Mother of my Lord, full of sorrow and most worthy of great pity, standing by the cross with the disciple whom Jesus loved. Finally I saw this also: how one of the impious men ran up, thrust a lance into his side, and immediately abundant blood flowed forth together with water. And behold, a thick and dreadful darkness arose over the whole earth; and rocks throughout the fields seemed terribly to crash together, collide, and split apart.

When that disturbance had ceased, behold, certain venerable men approached, took the body down from the cross, and carried it reverently into a green and pleasant garden. Wrapping it in a clean shroud, they placed it in a tomb. Then at last [Col. 0149C], recovering myself, I took up this lament with most bitter weeping: “Our shepherd, the fountain of living water, has departed; at his passing the sun was darkened.” And I added: “Hail, Mary, companion of martyrs, pierced through by the blood of your crucified son.” And I added: “When the Lord was buried, the tomb was sealed.”

57. After this, on Saturday at vespers, while I was in ecstasy, certain venerable women appeared to me, as though carrying spices. On holy Easter Day, when dawn had already come, I sat in my place of prayer and read in the Psalms. As I was approaching the end of the Psalms, I entered ecstasy and saw the garden in which the tomb was, the stone removed from its entrance, and angels sitting there. [Col. 0149D] And behold, a certain woman came, approached the tomb weeping, looked inside, and, not finding the body there, withdrew a little, as though sorrowful.

But the Lord met her; immediately she stopped, as though asking him something. Soon afterward she turned to return to the tomb; then suddenly she turned again, as though called by him, and ran and fell at his feet. When he had disappeared, she rose and quickly ran to the [Col. 0150A] house where the disciples were gathered and told them.

Immediately afterward, when I had recovered my breath a little, I saw two women coming to the sepulchre with spices. When they saw the angels, they stopped as though stunned. Then they approached more closely in fear; after waiting there briefly, they departed. The Lord also met them on the road; immediately they ran up, fell before him, and held his feet. This, however, was by no means seen of the woman mentioned above.

58. After this, while Mass was being celebrated, I saw two disciples hurrying to the sepulchre; one appeared older and the other younger. The latter, having arrived at the tomb first, did not enter; but the elder, upon arriving, immediately [Col. 0150B] entered, and afterward the other did also.

And what more do you ask, brother? Almost everything which the Gospels record as having happened at that time was shown to me. For I also saw how, when two men were going from Jerusalem to Emmaus, the Lord joined them in the appearance of a traveler; and how, when they reached the village and he pretended that he would go farther, they detained him and brought him into the house. When he sat down to dine, blessed the bread, and broke it, the place where he had been sitting immediately appeared empty. At once they rose and hurried to the disciples, reporting it to them in the house where they were gathered. At that very hour, while they were telling them these things, the Lord appeared [Col. 0150C] standing in their midst.

After this I saw also how he ate with them. There was on the table one dish containing fish and another containing a honeycomb. The garments in which I saw him after the resurrection were exceedingly white; his face was very joyful and of such brightness that I could scarcely look upon it.

59. On the feast of the Lord’s Ascension, at Mass, while I was in my ecstasy, I saw the disciples gathered in a house, with the Mother of the Lord among them. The Lord entered to them; and, after taking food with them, led them out of the city as far as the mountain. And I saw how he was raised up before their eyes. A multitude of angels came to meet him, and he was lifted up into heaven. While they stood looking [Col. 0150D] into heaven, two radiant young men appeared, coming down from above, and addressed them. Immediately they returned to the city and gathered themselves in the house from which they had gone out.

[Note: [Col. 0150D] The Lord’s Ascension was celebrated on 13 May; Pentecost, on 23 May.]

Then I returned to myself with words such as these: “The Lord led his disciples out as far as Bethany,” and what follows in the Gospel; and also: “O King of glory, Lord of hosts, who today as conqueror hast ascended above all the heavens.”

[Col. 0151A] 60. After this, on the day of Pentecost, before the celebration of Mass, while I was in ecstasy, I again saw the disciples gathered in the house mentioned above, with the Savior’s Mother among them. And while they sat, there appeared above each of them something like a flame of fire, descending from above in a violent rush. Immediately they all rose together and went out with great joy and confidence to proclaim the word of God among the people.

Having clearly seen these things, I was restored to myself, and at once uttered these words: “The Holy Spirit proceeding from the throne invisibly penetrated the breasts of the apostles.”

When the office of Mass was begun, I again entered ecstasy and saw a most brilliant beam of light extending from heaven to the altar. Through the middle [Col. 0151B] of it came the beautiful dove which I am accustomed to see, carrying in its beak something red, like a flame of fire, rather larger than usual. First it settled, its wings spread, upon the priest’s head, and there deposited from what it carried in its beak something like a single drop. It did the same to the ministers of the altar who were vested for reading; afterward it settled upon the altar.

When I returned from ecstasy, I told our mistress to remind the sisters to pray devoutly, hoping for the very thing which afterward occurred. When Mass had ended and we approached to receive communion, I entered ecstasy; and as they communicated one by one, I saw the aforesaid dove fly up and distribute to each from that which it carried in its beak.

[Col. 0151C] 61. These, brother, are the mercies of the Lord which he worked in me in the first year of my visitation.

[Note: [Col. 0151D] It seems rather that “the second year” should have been said, and that the third begins from this point, as is clear from what has been set forth thus far.]

But at the return of this second year, nearly the same things happen as used to happen around me in the preceding year on the feasts of saints; and there are also certain further matters, which we for the most part pass over in silence because of unbelievers. At times, too, words of a different kind from those usual are put into my mouth when I return from ecstasy, so that in speaking I follow not my own will but the Lord’s, who by my mouth makes manifest visions which, out of modesty, I had been accustomed to conceal from the sisters.

Thus, on the feast of Blessed Lawrence, he made known the vision I had seen in these words: “I saw a most noble deacon, Lawrence [Col. 0151D], standing before the gates, holding a palm; his crown was red, and he turned toward me, looking kindly upon me.”

Likewise, on the Assumption of our most blessed Lady, when I returned from my ecstasy, I suddenly began to speak thus before everyone: “I saw, above the heaven of heavens toward the east, many thousands of crowned saints—I judged them to be more than one hundred and forty-four thousand—all crowned with golden crowns, each one [Col. 0152A] according to his profession; and in their midst a most lofty and glorious throne. In the middle of the throne sat one whose face was terrible; from him and from the throne there issued a great splendor like flashing lightning, so that because of the excessive brightness I could scarcely raise my eyes. Around the throne were many angels and four living creatures. All these stood around, fell down, and worshiped him who sat upon the throne, saying: ‘Glory and honor and blessing to him who sits upon the throne, who lives for ages of ages.’”

After this I added: “Hail, holy, gracious, and noble Virgin Mary. For you are gentle; you are sweet; you are the helper and comforter of all who trust in you. Help me, my Lady Mary, for my soul trusts in you. Pray for me to your only-begotten Son, [Col. 0152B] our Redeemer, that he may complete in me the work of his mercy.”

62. On the feast of All Saints, the angel of the Lord came to me and carried my spirit away from my body. Immediately I went with him, and he led me upward before the gate which is in the presence of the Lord. I looked in and saw many thousands of crowned saints standing and ministering to God, with four living creatures around the throne. Angels and archangels, cherubim and seraphim, stood before the throne of God; they fell down and worshiped, and said in a clear voice: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come.” Likewise the twenty-four elders fell upon their faces and worshiped him who lives [Col. 0152C] for ages of ages.

I also have something to report to you, brother, concerning the consecration of the church of Bonn, which was recently performed. As you informed me by letter, I prayed to the Lord; and, as he is accustomed to do, he opened my eyes on the first Vespers of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross. Among other things shown to me, I saw a ray of abundant light from heaven to that church, illuminating it wholly with immeasurable brightness. I also saw a multitude of angels descending in the same ray and moving among the ministers of the church throughout the entire time of the dedication. Everything was filled with such majesty that I could not look upon what was being done there without fear.

I remained continuously in this vision from the evening of the preceding day until the hour at which the office of dedication [Col. 0152D] was completed. Among the things done there I saw you, brother, standing at the lectern at Matins and reading one of the lessons.

63. It happened that one of our sisters living in the convent at Diersten died.

[Note: [Col. 0151D] Letter IX of Elizabeth is addressed to the sisters of the monastery of Diersten; but where this monastery is or was I have not yet discovered. I suspect that Dorsten, a town in Westphalia in the diocese of Cologne, is meant. [Col. 0152D] But whether there were then sisters there must be investigated.]

When her death was reported to us, and we undertook an affliction according to custom for the remedy of her soul, I saw the angel of the Lord [Col. 0153A] standing beside our mistress, through whose ministry the work of God was being performed.

[Note: [Col. 0152D] This custom of mutual suffrage indicates some special connection between the two monasteries. The “affliction” to be undertaken by each person, mentioned here, may, I think, be understood as the flagellation practiced by religious and commonly called “discipline.”]

At the same hour I also saw our most blessed Lady, as though standing in the region of the lower air and looking toward us. When our affliction was completed, the angel rose up to her, and together they returned to the heights.

It happened on the vigil of the Lord’s Nativity, at the time of the morning sacrifice, while I was in prayer, that the Lord opened my eyes. In the spirit I saw a man whose presence I had desired, hurrying from afar to behold the contest of my suffering. When he arrived as evening was already drawing near, I saw the angel of the Lord coming down from above, as though to help me. When he stood before me, I said to him: “My Lord, I am weary of enduring.” And he said [Col. 0153B] to me: “Be strong; be comforted; do not fail on the way.”

Soon afterward my flesh rested in ecstasy, and he lifted me up in spirit on high; and I contemplated the joy which God has prepared for those who love him, as in the preceding year. When, after a long ecstasy, I returned to myself, these words immediately flowed to my lips: “He descended from heaven, sent from the Father’s citadel; he entered our region through the Virgin’s ear, clothed in a purple robe; and he came forth through the golden gate, the light and glory of the whole fabric of the world.” And this: “From his hidden dwelling the Son of God descended; he came to seek and save those who desired him with their whole heart.”

And the angel of the Lord came to me and carried away my spirit, [Col. 0153C] as I have related concerning the feast of All Saints. Afterward I blessed the Lord, saying: “I give thanks to you, Lord, who sent your angel to me, who comforted me in my tribulation, because you alone consider toil and pain.”

64. On the day of the greater Mass, while I was again in my ecstasy and praying most devoutly for the common correction of the Church of the Lord, at the end of my prayer I asked the Lord to deign to show me what his will was concerning clergy and nuns who were not walking in the good way. As, my prayer being completed, I began to return to myself, my angel stood beside me. I said to him: “O sweetest and most loving young man, answer me concerning the matters which I asked of the Lord.” He said [Col. 0153D] to me:

“Cry aloud and say to the sinful nation, the people full of sin: ‘Woe! Woe to you who live under the power of the devil. Cease to act perversely; learn to do good. Otherwise, behold, I the Lord send my angel to strike among you; unless you turn from your wicked ways and repent [Col. 0154A] of evil deeds, I the Lord will fulfill my indignation upon you.’”

65. Nor can I now keep silent concerning the great condescension with which my Lady made my heart rejoice. While I was in the ecstasy mentioned above, I saw her at a distance in a certain house, as though lying upon a little bed and handling with her hands a most beautiful and lovable infant. When she had wrapped him in gleaming white swaddling-clothes, she laid him in a manger which seemed to be beside her; and shortly afterward, taking him up, she reclined him in her lap.

[Note: [Col. 0153D] The Greeks likewise paint the Mother of God, in panels representing the twelve mysteries of the Lord, lying like a woman in childbed within a little basket or wicker cradle fitted for such use. Nor is it absurd to think that Joseph, having entered the stable, borrowed something of this kind from nearby and that the Virgin accepted it—not to yield to necessity, but to conform to the custom of women in childbirth, since she wished in no respect to appear exceptional. The Greeks indeed paint her thus in the cave; but to our Elizabeth she is represented thus [Col. 0154D] in the house in which, according to the Gospel history, the infant was found with his mother by the Magi: that is, after she had moved there from the cave or stable, after the shepherds had reported what the angel had told them concerning the child Messiah. Yet according to our opinion, by which we believe the Magi came one year after the child’s birth, it would be inapt to imagine the Mother of God still lying down. Therefore the reader should refer back to annotation 46.]

Immediately thereafter I saw her in the kingdom of brightness, as Queen and Lady. I invoked her according to my custom and especially asked her on behalf of a certain intimate acquaintance of mine. He was in deacons’ orders, and I had often urged him [Col. 0154B] not to delay in advancing to the sacred order of the priesthood. But he, alleging various grounds for fear, confessed that he did not yet dare undertake so arduous a matter. Therefore, when I mentioned this very matter before my Lady in that invocation, she answered me in these words: “Say to my servant: ‘Do not fear. Do what you are going to do, and render an account of my service, which you ought to have performed for me and did not perform.’”

66. On the feast of St John the Evangelist, during the divine office, while I lay in my bed because of illness, the hand of the Lord came upon me there; and I saw that beloved priest of the Lord standing in the presence of the throne. I therefore poured out prayers [Col. 0154C] to him and asked that I might be permitted to see something of those things which had been shown to him while he was upon earth. Immediately I saw four living creatures standing there, in the manner in which they are described in Ezekiel, and before them a fourfold wheel.

Then, as I was about to return to myself, I saw two angels sitting in the lower air, terrible and angry in countenance. One of them held in his right hand a dreadful sword extended as though to strike. I said to my guide: “My Lord, who are these?” He said: “They have authority to harm the earth.”

67. After this, on the day of the Innocents, I saw a great multitude of white-robed youths walking on a high mountain with emblems of martyrdom. They were preceded by [Col. 0154D] the white Lamb, bearing the sign of the cross. I said to my guide: “My Lord, who are these whom I see here?” He answered: “They are the innocent and undefiled, who follow the Lamb wherever he goes.” And I said: “Lord, why these more than others?” He replied: “Not only these: there are also others who are [Col. 0155A] innocent and undefiled, including virgins chosen in Christ.---Why the Lamb more than another animal?” He added: “Because the innocent, undefiled, and chosen Lamb was slain for the salvation of the human race.”

## CHAPTER V. Visions of the Year 1155, with an Appendix Relating to the Sixtieth Year

68. On the Epiphany of the Lord also, the Lord multiplied his grace in me. In the spirit I saw my Lady and her little child dwelling, as though in a house situated far away. And behold, three men of royal appearance entered there and, bending their knees, worshiped before the child. One of them brought forth a large gold coin, as though stamped with a royal image, and offered it into his hands. [Col. 0155B] Likewise the other two approached and reverently offered their gifts in certain vessels.

After this, the wedding which took place at Cana of Galilee was also represented to me. Again I saw the Savior there with Mary his mother reclining among the guests, and six water-jars set there. Moreover, the Lord did not disdain to show his handmaid the washing of his virginal body which was celebrated in the Jordan. For I saw how he descended with his holy Baptist into the waters of the blessed river, was baptized by him, and how a dove descended from heaven, came, and rested on his head. Awakening from this vision, I opened my mouth with these words: “In the form of a dove the Holy Spirit [Col. 0155C] was seen; the Father’s voice was heard: ‘This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him’ (Matt. XVII).”

69. After this, on the feast of the Purification, at first Vespers, God did something new and unusual to me. For while I was in my ecstasy as usual, praying in spirit to the Lord, greeting my Lady whom I beheld in the spirit, and pouring out devout prayers before her, the sisters who were around me openly heard the whole course of my prayer. But when I returned to myself, I refused to believe those who told me this, until they repeated in order the very words which I had used in prayer.

70. It also happened that an elderly sister [Col. 0155D] among us fell ill with the illness from which she died. On the third day before her death, her illness suddenly became so severe that we thought she was about to die; we ran to her and began the litany over her. Then ecstasy of mind rushed upon me. A little later, awakening, I said: “Anoint her,” for she had not yet been anointed with oil. Having said this, I immediately was in the spirit.

Again, soon afterward, awakening, before I had fully returned to myself, I declared aloud, in the hearing of all, the vision I had seen, [Col. 0156A] saying: “Our Lady descended with our Father St Benedict, and for some reason I do not know they immediately returned to the heights. And now many evil spirits have been present here, some of whom still walk about us like dogs and sit upon the roofs like vultures. But two angels stood beside the bed of our sister and said to them: ‘Depart from here; this sister has received a further span of life.’”

When I had said these things and fully returned to myself, I did not know that I had disclosed the vision. Calling our mistress aside, I began to tell her privately what I had seen; but she confessed that she had heard all the same things from my mouth. Three days later, when that sister departed this life, at the hour of her passing I saw in the spirit the same two [Col. 0156B] angels standing by her and receiving the soul as it left the body; but where they carried it was not revealed to me. While we prayed around the bier, I saw a beautiful angel, as though of small stature, seated on the top of the coffin. He did not move from there even when it was carried to the church of the brethren, and he remained until the time of burial.

71. After this, a severe fever seized me, and I desired the sacrament of Anointing. At that time the lord abbot had gone to nearby places, and I awaited his return. One evening around twilight, while our mistress sat before me, a certain venerable man came and stood before me. I thought he was the lord [Col. 0156C] abbot and rejoiced. As I rebuked his delay and harshness of manner, he kindly accepted the rebuke and comforted me, saying that I was not yet going to die.

I asked him to recite the Lord’s Prayer and the Creed before me and then anoint me. When he had done so, and I had responded at intervals to each word, he seemed to complete the entire rite of Anointing for me. Having given me his blessing, he departed. Our mistress, who had heard every word, asked with whom I had spoken. I said: “Was not the lord abbot present and did he not anoint me?” But she testified that she had seen no one there. Then, therefore, I first understood that I had seen a spiritual vision.

[Col. 0156D] 72. As the feast of the Annunciation drew near, I fell into a most serious illness and lay sick for two days before the feast day.

[Note: [Col. 0155D] In the year 1155 the dominical letter was B; Easter fell on 27 March. Therefore the feast of the Annunciation, since otherwise it would have coincided with Good Friday, had to be moved back according to the rubric of these dioceses, which in the Mainz usage reads: “If the feast of the Annunciation [Col. 0156D] falls on Saturday, it is to be celebrated solemnly in choir and in public; but if it falls after Palm Sunday or in Easter Week, it is anticipated on the vigil of Palm Sunday in the manner set out above.” Thus in that year this feast was celebrated on 19 March.]

On the morning of the feast day itself my illness became so severe that the sisters came to my bed and said the litany over me. As they were about to leave, they asked whether I wished to communicate that day, as they themselves were about to do. But I refused, saying that, because of the weakness [Col. 0157A] of my body, I had not prepared myself by worthy works for this as they had. They were saddened and left me. Then the angel of the Lord came, stood before me, put his hand upon my head, and said: “Rise and stand upon your feet. You have been freed from your illnesses. Come forward to communicate; be strengthened and be strong.”

At these words all illness immediately fled from me, and throughout my whole body I was most sweetly relieved. I added: “It would indeed have been possible, Lord, to make the sufferings which you have endured until now lighter for yourself. But, that you might be more fully believed, you chose to be afflicted in this manner.”

Immediately, taking hold of my clothes, I rose from my bed, descended in full strength and with a lively complexion, came joyfully into the gathering of sisters—to the amazement of all—and did what he had commanded me.

That same day the Lord’s Annunciation was also presented to me. For in the spirit I saw my Lady standing in prayer as though in a certain chamber; suddenly an angel of great brightness appeared before her, seemingly speaking with her. At the sight of him she seemed frightened; after their mutual conversation, she reverently bowed toward him, and immediately he disappeared.

73. On the day before Palm Sunday, as evening was already drawing near, I stood alone in the oratory, intent on prayer. Behold, a ray of abundant light was suddenly poured down from heaven upon me, producing in me a heat like that of the sun when it shines in its strength. I fell to the ground and entered into ecstasy of mind. The sisters came running [Col. 0157C] to me, wishing to lift my head from the ground and place cushions beneath it, but they could not raise it by any effort.

Soon afterward the angel of the Lord came, swiftly raised me, and set me upon my feet, saying: “O human being, rise and stand upon your feet, and I shall speak with you. Do not fear, for I am with you all the days of your life. Act manfully; let your heart be strengthened; wait for the Lord. And you shall say to the transgressors of the earth: ‘Thus says the Lord: As nations once crucified me, so am I daily crucified among those who have transgressed against me in their hearts. For they turn their faces from me, and their heart is far from me, so that they may neither see nor reflect upon how I suffered and how I redeemed them in my blood [Col. 0157D]. And you shall say to them: Return, transgressors, to the Lord your God, for he is kind and merciful, who does not will the death of the sinner but rather that he should turn and live.’”

When he had said these things, he departed. I signaled to the sisters to bring writing tablets and take these words down in writing, for I could say nothing else until everything had been written down according to my narration.

74. Again, on Palm Sunday itself, during the divine office, when I similarly entered into ecstasy of mind, the angel raised me up and said: “O human being, consider what you are: dust and ashes, a fragile creature. Hear me who speak with you. Thus says the Lord: ‘The earth is full of wickedness, and this people is not my people, but a people hostile to me. Their heart has been hardened; they will not receive nor be able to understand the words which I have spoken, but will depart from me. Woe to them, because they are oppressed by the devil, obey him, dishonor my face by their evil deeds, and have forgotten God their maker.’”

And I said: “My Lord, I do not know what to say or what to do, for I am unlearned in the divine Scriptures.” And he said to me: “My grace is sufficient for you; for to him who has, it shall be given, and from him who has not, even that which he has shall be taken away.”

After this, on Monday, as I attended Matins, the Lord put this word in my mouth: “Woe to you, hypocrites, who hide gold and silver—that is, the word of God and the law of the Lord, which is more precious than gold and silver—so that you may appear religious and innocent to men; but inwardly [Col. 0158B] you are full of evil contrivance and your uncleannesses, while entering into the Holy of Holies, that is, the altar of God, to communicate. Truly the Lord turns away his face so as not to see your burnt offerings and sacrifices. You are more miserable than those who look at you as at a mirror when they consider your evil works and are scandalized by you. Know for certain that in this time the law will perish first from the priests and elders of the people.”

75. Likewise, on Wednesday, when I was alone in the chapter-house, I came into ecstasy. And the angel of the Lord said to me: “And you, son of man, shall say to those who dwell upon the earth: Hear, peoples: the God of gods has spoken. Repent, for the kingdom of God is near; and turn to me with your whole heart, and I [Col. 0158C] the Lord will turn to you and be reconciled with you. But if you refuse, and provoke me to anger, you shall die in your sins, and death shall suddenly devour you, as though unaware; and you shall be more wretched than every creature, even than brute animals, which, once dead, suffer no further evil; but you shall be tormented in eternal fire, where there shall be weeping of eyes and grinding of teeth without end.”

And I said: “Lord, I do not know how to speak, and I am slow in speaking.” And he said: “Open your mouth, and I will speak; and whoever hears you hears me.”

On Holy Saturday before Easter, I was going to the chapter-house and came into ecstasy on the threshold of the chapel, and a light shone around me. And the angel of the Lord, standing beside me, said:

[Col. 0158D] “O most wretched persons, who heap up treasures for yourselves in infernal punishments. Do you not know how many nobles, how many powerful persons, will perish on the day of judgment; how many rich and wise persons will mourn? O glory of the world, a wretched thing! Woe to those who love it! I cried out, says the Lord, and again I cry out: who is there to hear me and assent to my counsels? When I cried out, I cried out and said: If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink, and living waters shall flow from his belly. O man, whoever you are, say: ‘Behold, here I am’; and it shall be said to you: ‘Deny yourself; and, made obedient and humble in heart, come and follow me, and I shall test whether you are true or not.’ And you, being steadfast and persevering, do not fail in the contest; for whoever has contended well unto the end shall be saved.”

[Col. 0159A]

76. On one of the Easter days at noon, as I wished to rest, the angel of the Lord stood by my bed and said to me: “Do not be troubled over the things that are accustomed to happen to you; my grace is sufficient for you, because I shall not abandon you unless you yourself wish it. Strive to be obedient with all humility and gladness of heart. Be patient against every adversity; do not exalt yourself in pride, but always humble yourself in order that you may be exalted. Despise no one, scorn no one; show a good example in all things. You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and your neighbour as yourself; and what I have given you, give to others also, that they too may be refreshed; for you would not have it unless it had been given you from above.”

Besides these and many other things, which he added while kindly instructing me as a father instructs a child, [Col. 0159B] alas, escaped my memory because sleep intervened.

77. On the feast of St Mark the Evangelist [Note: [Col. 0159D] St Mark, 25 April, which that year fell on the Monday of the Fourth Sunday after Easter.], I saw a door opened in heaven, and a great brightness was poured out from it upon me, and I immediately came into ecstasy. While I was in that rapture, I saw before the throne of God—as I had seen on the feast of Blessed John the Evangelist—four living creatures, each having four faces, which I observed arranged as follows. The face of a man was on the front side, facing the throne; on the back was the face of an eagle; on the right, the face of a lion; and on the left, the face of a calf. They also had six wings each. Two of these, raised above the head of each creature, were joined together; [Col. 0159C] two were spread out, so that one wing of each touched the wing of another; and with two they covered their bodies. They were full of eyes before and behind.

There also appeared a great and shining wheel, standing before them, before the throne, as though encompassing four wheels. These were so joined to one another that each enclosed the two adjacent to it on either side, while all touched the greater wheel inwardly with their circles. There was a certain space among the four, about the central point of the greater wheel, reddish like the flame of fire; and from it certain little sparks seemed to issue and scatter through all the wheels, which seemed to be enlivened from it. Therefore, in that same hour, these words came to my mind: “The spirit of life was in the wheels.” And as I looked, the living creatures separated from one another into four directions, and each was preceded by its own wheel.

[Col. 0159D]

78. On a certain Sunday, while Mass was being celebrated among the brothers, I happened to look out through a window, wishing to hear the brothers singing glory to God. A certain man happened to be standing in the road, shouting at another and saying: “Why are you lingering there so long now, devil?” Immediately I saw Satan in the form of a black and misshapen calf, standing beside him. By this, the faithful are warned to refrain from such malicious words.

On the day of Pentecost [Note: [Col. 0160D] Pentecost fell on 15 May that year.], certain solemnities of Mass had been suspended among us because of the count’s excommunication; [Col. 0160A] nevertheless, the Lord did not suspend his consolation from his handmaids. For one of the priests came to us carrying in a pyx the sacrament of the Lord’s Body, from which we were, according to custom, to communicate. When he had been admitted and had placed the pyx upon the altar within our enclosure, I saw a great light coming forth from heaven, directed upon it like a ray of the sun, illuminating it wholly. A snow-white dove also seemed to come flying through the midst of that same light and settled beside it. The angel of the Lord came also and stood beside the altar, as if a witness to our devotion, until all of us had communicated in order.

79. On the Sunday night [Note: [Col. 0160D] Then 16 June.] before the feast [Col. 0160B] of the Apostles Peter and Paul, while I stood in the place of prayer, I came into an ecstasy which I would gladly have resisted, had I been able. Immediately the angel of the Lord stood before me and said in our own language: “O wretched woman, why do you suffer these things so unwillingly? How many there are who would gladly endure them, if they were granted to attain what you attain! If you do not suffer these things now, you shall certainly suffer there, where you must suffer more harshly, before you are permitted to see what you are now going to see.”

And I said: “My Lord, this impatience comes to me from my great frailty; and, if you wish to console me, Lord, what will you show me?” And he said: “Come and see, and contemplate the delight that shall come to you from your God.”

Immediately he lifted me up into the high air, [Col. 0160C] and I looked through a door of brightness and saw, as usual, the glory of the blessed city of God. I was again brought back to my wretched body and took a little breath. Then I was again in the spirit and saw before that aforesaid door something like a balance hanging there. My angel stood there, holding one book, and Satan another. I understood the book held by the angel to be the book of my righteous deeds, and the other to be the book of my offences. Each placed the book he held in the balance, and the book of offences appeared to outweigh the other. The angel therefore stood as though sorrowful and said: “It shall not be so, because she has endured many great pains for her offences and has often received harsh scourging.” And when [Col. 0160D] he had mentioned many further things of this sort, he said: “These matters must be deferred until tomorrow.”

I was at once restored to myself, and with abundant tears I cried out: “Do not enter into judgment with your handmaid, Lord; but I beseech your mercy that you forgive my sins before you come to judge at the judgment.”

80. As I was oppressed by excessive anxiety, the angel again presented himself to me. And I said to him: “Lord, instruct me, my Lord, what I am to do.” He said: “Be very obedient, humble, patient, and loving. Gladly endure these things that happen to you. Embrace with love the things which the Lord works in you, [Col. 0161A] and grant prayers to those who love you, to all who have entrusted themselves to your sisters, and to those to whom you have bound yourself by promise.”

Having said this, he departed. Yet I continued to be troubled in my heart and began to consider these things within myself, saying: “Have I not always had great confidence in the Body of my Lord Jesus Christ? Is this not the remission of all sins? There certainly I shall take refuge.” Therefore I asked the mistress to send a messenger swiftly and request the lord abbot to celebrate, on the following day, the Mass of the Holy Trinity and bring the divine sacrament to me. For I feared that I should die that day, because of the angel’s words, when he had said, “These matters must be deferred until tomorrow.”

81. Therefore, while, as I had asked, he was celebrating Mass, [Col. 0161B] at the very time of the sacrifice I came into an ecstasy of mind and again saw the balance that I had seen in the evening, with the books placed upon it. Then the angel came, my faithful advocate, bringing something like a small piece of bread, such as priests use in the celebration of Masses, and laid it upon the book of my righteous deeds. Immediately, as though he had placed upon it an enormous mass, it appeared swiftly to outweigh the book in the other pan.

Awakening with joy, I cried: “Holy Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, into the hands of your power, into the hands of your mercy, I commend my spirit, my purpose, my thoughts, and my whole body; my life, my end, and all my actions. May your blessing always be [Col. 0161C] upon me by day and by night, and may your mercy lead me into eternal life.”

I also added this, because I was about to communicate: “Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but save me, and I shall be saved, for you are my praise. May I be worthy to receive your Body and Blood, not unto judgment, but unto the remission of all my sins.”

At that same time I saw in the spirit the lord abbot in the church of the brothers, devoutly consecrating the saving sacrament, with a dove present beside the sacrifice and the brightness of light surrounding it. Afterwards he came to me, bringing what I had desired, and I consoled my soul by holy communion.

82. Again, on the vigil of the Apostles, at Vespers, [Col. 0161D] I saw them in the spirit in a region of brightness, and with them the Mother of the Lord. I also saw the same balance that I had seen before, and the books were placed upon it. A multitude of demons stood around one pan and a multitude of angels around the other, and the weights appeared equal.

Then I invoked my Lady and the Apostles with great anguish, because I believed without doubt that I was going to die. They withdrew inward for a little while. When they appeared again, and I did not cease to invoke them and several other saints, the book of righteousness appeared to outweigh the other. Afterwards, as I drew breath, my angel came to me and said: “Space for living has been granted you; make your life more reformed.”

And I said: “My Lord, what more shall I do? Do you not [Col. 0162A] know my frailty, and how I cannot labour more than I do?” Then he instructed me and exhorted me to a certain affliction of the flesh, concerning which I too had often deliberated within myself.

Returning to myself, I said: “Peter, at God’s command, loose the chains of the earth”; and, besides this, other prayers to him. And I added: “Holy Paul the Apostle, preacher of truth and teacher of the nations, intercede for us with the Lord who chose you.” To these I added: “Lord, do not judge me, wretched and sinful as I am, according to my deed; for I have done nothing worthy in your sight. Therefore I beseech your majesty that you, O God, may blot out my iniquity, because you formed me from the earth.” And this: “Do not deliver to the beasts a soul confessing you, [Col. 0162B] and do not forget forever the souls of your poor.”

That day, at Mass, the Apostles again appeared to me, and Our Lady with them. Then I also saw in the spirit the brothers ministering in church, and the lord abbot standing at the altar, and I described to the sisters the appearance of his chasuble. That same day, when the divine sacrament was brought to us, I saw the same vision that I had seen on the day of Pentecost.

83. Here is the end of the visions brought down to July of the year 1155. To these I would add one from the book of letters, certainly assigned to no year, but earlier than the final item of this book, which concerns the year 1159. It is chapter V of the aforesaid book and reads as follows:

“To Lord G. (Gerlach), venerable [Col. 0162C] abbot of the church of God at Tuitio, Elizabeth of Schönau, humble handmaid of Christ, greeting and prayers.

“Be comforted and rejoice in the Lord, and strengthen the hearts of the brothers who are with you, because the Lord has received your groans and looked upon the affliction of your heart, by which you were distressed in his sight because of the lamentable loss of the Lord’s sacrament that occurred in your midst. For, according to the custom of his kindness, he acted and deigned to announce to me through his angel certain words from which you may receive consolation.

“It happened on the first Sunday of Lent, while the lord abbot was celebrating the divine office among us. After the reading of the Gospel I suddenly became faint and came into an ecstasy of mind. And behold, the angel of the Lord, my kindly [Col. 0162D] comforter, came and stood before me. Then, among the other conversations that I had with him, I made mention of you before him, as I had been prompted by my brother, and I asked him, saying: ‘My Lord, what became of that venerable sacrament which was shaken from the throat of a sneezing boy in the church of Tuitio? Was it trampled under the feet of those standing around and lost?’

“He answered: ‘The holiness of that sacrament gives life to the spirit of the one who receives it; but what slipped from his mouth was received by the angel of God who stood present and was placed in a secret place.’

“And I said: ‘Lord, do I dare ask in what place it has been stored?’ And he said: ‘Do not ask.’

“Again I said: ‘Lord, what service is fitting for those brothers to perform?’ And he answered: ‘For forty days the sacrifice of praise shall be offered to God in the community for this offence.’

“I further added, saying: ‘In our Lord’s stead I establish this satisfaction: wherever the Body of the Lord falls upon the ground, or the Lord’s Blood is spilled, so that it cannot afterward be put among the relics, the sacrifice of praise shall be offered for this offence for forty days; but if it can be put among the relics, the same shall be done for thirty days.’

“Finally he added this also: ‘It is expedient and necessary for those brothers that, the more they gather holy bodies to themselves and place them beside them, the more earnestly they should endeavour to minister to them honourably and lovingly, and amend their lives with the fear of God [Col. 0163B] and observe their rule more diligently. For the Lord permitted what happened in their midst in order to admonish them of this. But if they obey his warning and do what I have said, let them be certain that those precious martyrs will intercede for them before the Lord and will aid them in every necessity; but if they do not, they will bring accusation and complaint against them.’”

84. Let the reader understand these martyrs as those of the Ursulan company, and understand their founder, Heribert, bishop of Cologne, himself buried there. Now let the reader also receive an Appendix, added by some writer—I do not know how—to Book II, which, as I have said, ends with the Visions of the year 1156; it forewarns the Saint of a future coincidence of the days of the Annunciation and the Passion [Col. 0163C] of the Lord, which occurred in the year of the Incarnation 1160; from this it follows that the vision narrated in this Appendix belongs to July 1159. It is as follows:

“It happened also on one of the days of July. I, Elizabeth, had withdrawn to a remote and secluded place and was occupied in prayer; and behold, the angel of the Lord came and stood before me, and said: ‘Do you not know that in the coming year Easter must be celebrated on the very day upon which the Lord rose, and that the feast of the Annunciation [Note: [Col. 0163D] Namely, in the year 1160, under the same recurrence of the dominical letter B noted above. By these words of the angel, either Henschenius’s opinion is confirmed, which places Christ’s death in year 29 of the common era, [Col. 0164D] and on 25 March; or, if Christ was not in fact crucified on that day, a new argument is proved for what I have taught elsewhere: that God and angels speaking to ecstatic saints use words suited to their understanding.] will fall upon the day of the Passion?’

“I was silent, because I truly did not know this. And he continued, saying: ‘Know that at that time Satan shall receive from God the power to incite human beings against one another, so that they may kill one another. [Col. 0163D] The sun shall be suffused with redness and veiled in darkness. This will be nothing other than much shedding of blood and immense sorrow among the Christian people. After this, a serpent, an emitter of corruption, shall invisibly kill human beings, and there shall be great tribulation on earth; so that everyone who escapes with life unharmed shall owe the Lord perpetual praise. But if I were to recount to you what is soon to come after these things, I know that you would not be able to endure because of the greatness of your fear.’”

85. It is plainly evident that these threats began to be fulfilled in the year 1160, for which, as I have said, they were foretold. [Col. 0164A] For in that year, when Adrian IV died in September and Alexander III was elected, the antipope Octavian rose up at Rome under the name Victor. Having gained the emperor Frederick as his supporter, he stirred up the most destructive schism in Italy and Germany—not even to be ended by his death, but to be continued, as others were successively elected after him, until the year 1177. While the schism lasted and Frederick persecuted the pope in Italy, that most severe mortality arose which Baronius describes under the year 1166, no. 11, and which seems to be threatened here.

Upon considering everything, it might seem that this item was added to this book because the third book which follows in the edition, although it concerns the year 1156, seemed properly to follow the second; yet it was separately transmitted [Col. 0164B] and is praised by Trithemius in his book *On Writers* as a most beautiful and not useless work, and in the Chronicle of Hirsau as a beautiful and necessary work. Then, in the Chronicle of Sponheim, he praises Egbert because, while a monk at Schönau and afterwards abbot, he recast all the writings and revelations of the holy Sister into the more elegant style and form in which they are now read. Moreover, the letter addressed to St Hildegard, which we have appended to the preface, seems to concern the threats directed against the Christian world in this Appendix as already beginning to be made public; and thus also Elizabeth’s appointment as teacher, to which she was elected about the same time.

## CHAPTER VI. Beginning of the Book of the Ways of God, begun to be written in 1156, and summary of the discourses contained in it

[Col. 0164C]

86. This is the Book of the Ways of God, which was announced by the angel of God Most High to Elizabeth, handmaid of Christ and of the living God, in the fifth year of her visitation, in which the Spirit visited her for the salvation of all who receive with grateful blessing the fatherly admonitions of God. It was in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1156.

At the beginning of the fifth year of my visitation, as the feast day of Pentecost was approaching, I, Elizabeth, saw in a vision of my spirit a high mountain, brightly illuminated in abundance at its summit, and as it were three ways extending from its foot to its peak. One of these—the middle one—was set directly before me and had the appearance of a clear sky or of a hyacinth stone; [Col. 0164D] the one on my right appeared green, and that on my left purple. At the top of the mountain, opposite the middle way, stood a distinguished man clothed in a hyacinth-coloured tunic and girded about the loins with a white belt. His face shone like the sun, his eyes radiated like stars, and his hair was like the whitest wool. He had in his mouth a two-edged sword, in his right hand a key, and in his left something like a royal sceptre.

87. In another vision, on the solemnity of Pentecost, [Col. 0165A] I saw on the ascent of that same mountain, to the left of the aforesaid man and alongside the ways of the earlier vision, three other paths possessing the following different appearances. One of them, which appeared nearer to the green path, was pleasant indeed, but was so enclosed and covered on every side by dense brambles that those walking through it had necessarily to be pricked by them, unless they walked carefully restrained and bent low. There also appeared a delightful path, narrow and apparently little trodden, with no brambles, but abundantly bordered on both sides by pleasant grass and flowers of various kinds. Between these two was another path, wider than the others, level, and as though paved with red bricks. As I looked upon it more attentively, the angel of the Lord standing beside me [Col. 0165B] said: “You see this path, and it seems beautiful to you and convenient for walking; but it is dangerous, and those who walk along it easily slip.”

88. Again, on the Octave of Pentecost, during the noon rest, the eyes of my heart were suddenly opened, without bodily affliction, as also in the visions mentioned above, and I again saw all the things previously described. Moreover, the Lord showed me, besides the paths I had seen, four others alongside the three paths of the first vision, to the right of the man standing at the summit of the mountain. One of them, nearest to the purple path, appeared difficult up to the middle of the mountain because of the density of brambles that covered it on either side. The remainder [Col. 0165C] of it as far as the summit appeared pleasant with flowers and free from impediments, but narrow and little trodden. The path next to this appeared dry, like a ploughed field, rough with great clods of earth, and extremely burdensome to its travellers.

As I was considering these two paths and thinking that they made progress difficult, the angel standing by me answered and said: “If anyone walks on these paths, let that person beware lest his foot stumble. But whoever stumbles and falls, if he does not rise but remains there, shall not see the eternal light.” The other two paths, which appeared alongside these, were level and easy and beautiful to behold, having the whiteness of ground well worn down on a public roadway. As I lingered [Col. 0165D] in looking at them, I again heard the angel say: “The way of the righteous has been made straight, and the path of the saints prepared.”

89. The interpretation of the first vision, as I received it through the angel, is this. The high mountain is the height of heavenly blessedness; the light upon the summit of the mountain is the brightness of eternal life; the different paths on the mountain are the diverse ascents of the elect, by which they ascend to the kingdom of brightness.

The hyacinth path is the pursuit of divine contemplation. Those walk upon it who, in unceasing meditation and desire, fix the eye of the mind upon God and heavenly things. The green path belongs to those who strive to be perfect and blameless in the active life, walking without complaint in all the commandments of the Lord. Since, in all their works, they look not to a transient but to the unfading prize [Col. 0166A] of heavenly recompense, they set the steps of their minds in green.

The purple path is the ascent of blessed martyrs, who, carrying out the justice of God through patience amid the torments of their sufferings, strive to pass in the purple of their own blood to the divine light.

The distinguished man above the mountain is Christ. The brightness of his face is a sign of his divine splendour; his radiant eyes are his serene regard for the elect; his hair, like white wool, declares that he is the Ancient of Days, although in the last days he was born according to the flesh. The two-edged sword in his mouth is the sentence of terrible judgment that will issue from his mouth, striking the reprobate with a double destruction of body and soul. The key appeared in his right hand because he alone [Col. 0166B] opens the gate of life and no one shuts it; he shuts it and no one opens it (Rev. 3). He also unlocks the depths of God’s mysteries for whomever he wills, and there is no one who shuts them; he seals, and there is no one who can break the seal.
